  Description: ##### Overview
    The catch-all FastAPI exception handler returns `str(exc)` and `traceback.format_exc()` in the 500 response body for any unhandled error on any route, including unauthenticated ones.
    
    ##### Applicability
    SI-11 (error messages without revealing exploitable information; detailed errors only to authorized personnel). The handler is registered for `Exception` app-wide, so every endpoint in this service is in scope.
    
    ##### Evidence
    `main.py` lines 32-35 register the handler and serialize the exception message and stack trace into the JSON response. No logging of the error server-side occurs, and no generic message is substituted. Any input that raises (e.g. a malformed SQL fragment in `/assets/{name}` reaching `db.find_asset`) returns file paths, module names, SQL text and line numbers to the caller.
    
    ##### Impact
    - Internal source paths, library versions, SQL statements and CUI-adjacent data in exception messages are disclosed to any client.
    - Combined with the SQL concatenation in `db.find_asset`, error output aids injection exploitation.
    - The error is also not written to the audit/log stream, so the event is lost server-side.
  Recommendation: Return a generic body such as {"error": "internal error", "id": <correlation id>} with status 500, and log the traceback server-side (log.exception) with the correlation id. Add a regression test asserting no 'Traceback' text in 500 responses.

  Description: ##### Overview
    `TOKEN_SECRET` is read from the environment but defaults to the literal `change-me` when unset, so a missing env var silently makes every bearer token forgeable.

  Description: ##### Overview
    `/export` returns every asset record to any caller presenting the single static `X-API-Key`; it does not use `require_token`, has no role check, and cannot attribute access to an individual.

  Description: ##### Overview
    The `mrt` container sets `privileged: true` and `runAsUser: 0`, and omits `runAsNonRoot`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, capability drops and a seccomp profile.
    
    ##### Applicability

    The `audit()` helper writes `AUDIT <event> <detail>` through a logger configured with format `%(message)s`, so records carry no time, source address, actor identity or outcome field.
    
    ##### Applicability
    AU-3 a-f and AU-3(1) with the ISSM-defined fields in `docs/il5/00-boundary.md` (actor, action, object, source IP, UTC time, outcome). The boundary doc lists AU-3/AU-3(1) as code-owned; storage/retention is inherited from the platform.

    - Failed-login records log the raw supplied username (could contain mistyped passwords).

    ##### Impact
    - A stolen or leaked token grants indefinite access to CUI via `/assets/{name}`.
    - No session-timeout events can be audited because none occur.
  Recommendation: Track sessions server-side (session id in token, last-activity timestamp in a store); reject and audit when now - last_activity > 15 min or now > exp, refresh last_activity on each request, and add a POST /logout that deletes the session. Set SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES=15.

findings.title: Dockerfile has no USER directive, so the mrt image runs as root
findings.raw:
- sfind-9c145066b20045ed8e044d118d7a3695: Dockerfile has no USER directive, so the mrt image runs as root [high/open] repo: achilli444/il5-uplift-demo, scan: scan-63e0dadf072843d78ef6f9b5515c55f8 created 2026-10-27 08:59:30 UTC, category: deviation
  Description: ##### Overview
    The `mrt` image built from `Dockerfile` never sets a non-root `USER`, so the uvicorn process runs as UID 0 (the `python:3.12-slim` default) unless the pod spec overrides it. `k8s/deployment.yaml` does not override it. It sets `runAsUser: 0` and `privileged: true` (lines 16-18), which another batch covers. Cluster-wide PSA admission is owned by the platform (docs/il5/00-boundary.md).
    
    ##### Applicability
    V-242437 (CAT I) requires a pod security policy. For Kubernetes 1.25 and later this means Pod Security Admission at the `restricted` level, which requires `runAsNonRoot: true`. The Dockerfile is the only in-repo artifact that sets the container's default user, so it is in scope. The namespace PSA label and the cluster admission config are not in this repo; that evidence must come from the platform team's cluster configuration.
    
    ##### Evidence
    - Dockerfile lines 1-7 go from `FROM` to `CMD` with no `USER` instruction and create no non-root account. The image's default identity therefore stays root.
    - Under the `restricted` profile, a pod that sets `runAsNonRoot: true` with this image would be rejected by the kubelet, because the image has no non-root UID. A pod without that field runs as root.
    - k8s/deployment.yaml lines 16-18 explicitly set root and privileged mode, so nothing downstream corrects this.
    
    ##### Impact
    - The CUI-handling API process runs as root inside the container. Any code-execution flaw in the app (for example the SQL injection or debug handler seeded in `app/`) gives root in the container, and with `privileged: true` that extends to the node.
    - The image cannot run under PSA `restricted` without being rebuilt.
    - Not verified: whether the platform's admission controller (Kyverno/Gatekeeper in Big Bang) would block or mutate this pod at runtime.
  Recommendation: Create an unprivileged account and switch to it before CMD, for example `RUN groupadd -r -g 10001 mrt && useradd -r -u 10001 -g mrt mrt` with `COPY --chown=10001:10001 app ./app` and then `USER 10001` (use a numeric UID so `runAsNonRoot` can verify it). In k8s/deployment.yaml, set `runAsNonRoot: true`, `runAsUser: 10001`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` and `capabilities.drop: [ALL]`, and remove `privileged: true`. Port 8000 needs no root.
  Note: Aggregation: only deviation in this scan; no duplicates. Verified at 45da2de: Dockerfile lines 1-7 have no USER, and k8s/deployment.yaml:16-18 sets privileged: true and runAsUser: 0. The finding text says another batch covers those lines, but this scan has no finding for them. Fix both in one PR: add a numeric non-root USER in Dockerfile, and in the pod securityContext set runAsNonRoot/runAsUser 10001, allowPrivilegeEscalation false, drop ALL, and remove privileged. Sibling gaps in the repo that no finding covers (not created here, recorded for follow-up): k8s/deployment.yaml:19-21 has a plaintext secret in env TOKEN_SECRET (value [REDACTED]) that bears on V-242415/V-274883, and the Deployment declares no metadata.namespace, so it lands in default (V-242383). Out of scope (platform-inherited): cluster PSA namespace labels, admission controllers (Kyverno/Gatekeeper), and Service/NodePort exposure. Kept HIGH because the gap maps to CAT I V-242437 with root plus privileged in the in-repo manifests. No CODEOWNERS file. The only committer is Devin (seed commit 977214f).
